rows: Three things matter here. Turning up, listening, and knowing which of the first two you forgot.
Brawling: one, it works; two, it has a cost; three, you should know both before you start.
A risk: one, the probability; two, the cost; three, whether you are willing to pay it.
Pace: one, the plan; two, the reason; three, who is listening to it.
The people: one, they came; two, they paid; three, they deserve a clear result.
I know the standard, and I will hold to it.
Three things I can offer: a clear plan, a steady hand, and an honest account afterwards.
Stance: one, feet set; two, weight low; three, ready to move when the bell goes.
Technique, item one. Name the first step, the second step, and the reason for the third.
Strikes: one, the mechanics; two, the target; three, the reason you chose it.
A gamble without a plan has no value. Give me your plan in three points.
A stall: one, it wastes time; two, it annoys the crowd; three, it is not my method.
The people want a contest with three honest parts: a start, a middle and a finish.
You say I am irrelevant. I can list three ways I am still useful. Would you like them?
You are proud of your {strength}. Item one, as it happens. Okay. Here is the correction: it works only if the second half is sound.
I have listed your {strength}. One: it is real. Two: it has a gap. Three: I know where it is.
Calm, item two. Okay. That is one of the three things I expected you to do.
That lands, item three. That is the first correction agreed. We can move on.
I could list all the problems with that. I will mention only one.
One count, that is the list. Three conditions: clean, clear, and over before the bell. Keep me down and you meet them.
On the mat I will count every movement. One, two, three. Stay with me, step by step.
Grounded or standing, the rule is the same. Stay inside the standards.
Stay, and face me, next on the list. Show me one good move, then another, then a third.
A proper answer, in order. That is the first point I accept.
The question is item four, and still open. I asked for three things. You have given me none.
That lands, item three. Noted, and filed.
That I accept, as item one. We will settle the rest at the bell.
I will wrestle this match to the standard. One, I will be careful. Two, I will be honest. Three, I will finish.
My approach is methodical. You will see it on the night, in order.
Whatever happens, there will be a clear record of what happened.
There are two more items to come. There is one item left on the list.
I have one item left, and you will hear it when the bell rings.
There are two separate matters here. What I suspect, and what I can establish. I can only put the second on the record.
Point one: I owe you an example. Point two: I haven't got one. Strike that item from the discussion.
Item removed. Now we can discuss the work that actually needs doing.
That's a better account. Keep the speculation off the list and the match on it.
They'll see how we handle ourselves when there's nowhere to hide. That's the evidence I want.
We can show them who keeps working when the match gets difficult. The rest is talk.
